narrative.title: Why pharma, why now
narrative.body:
I spent the first part of my career in institutional finance, most recently at Goldman Sachs, managing 20+ institutional relationships across multi-million dollar syndicated loan portfolios. The real skill there wasn't the numbers. It was earning the trust of time-strapped people who had every other option available to them, reading what each one actually needed, and knowing dense, jargon-heavy contracts well enough to solve real problems with them. In 2023, I stepped back to raise my two kids.

In 2025, I watched a stranger save someone's life during a medical emergency, and it pushed me to earn my EMT license. I finished in the top 5% of my cohort at UT Dallas. During clinicals I worked in the emergency department, on patient transfers, and in the ambulance, including administering medication under protocol, and completed training in pharmacology fundamentals. What stayed with me was how often a patient's outcome traced back to whether the right medication had reached them, and whether the provider treating them had the right information at the right moment. That's the part of the chain a rep owns.

I've always been achievement-oriented and tenacious, and pharmaceutical sales is where those instincts and this clinical foundation actually converge. I know what I don't have: two years with a B2B outside sales title on my resume. What I do have is the underlying work that requirement screens for. As a full-time volunteer representative across Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota, I ran a three-state territory for 18 months with my own CRM pipeline, daily pre-call planning, post-call evaluations, and hard weekly targets. I built that territory from underperforming to one of the strongest in the region, and I did it by developing the community gatekeepers who could open doors a cold pitch never would. That is territory building, gatekeeper access, and rejection tolerance, learned the hard way rather than in a training program.

I also bring two things most candidates coming out of a traditional B2B seat don't. I'm clinically fluent, so I can hold a real conversation with a physician and their staff on day one rather than spending six months learning to. And I'm bilingual in Spanish, which across DFW physician offices means I can build genuine rapport with front office staff and gatekeepers, the people who decide whether you get five minutes or none.

I live in the DFW metro, my kids are in preschool with full-time childcare in place, and I'm looking for a territory where I can bring my hunger and grit. My approach is simple: know the product, know the territory, build real trusting relationships with the people in it, and keep pivoting until I find the right need and the right angle to close.
